info.title: LunchVoice API
info.description: Machine-readable contract for LunchVoice. v2 operations are Postgres functions behind PostgREST RPC returning a 200 envelope; legacy operations are the live v1 surface. Per-operation x-status says whether it exists: implemented (production), implemented-nonprod, proposed, blocked-decision. A null limit means undecided, never unlimited.

post.summary: Current account, accepted memberships with roles and advisory capabilities, and pending applications.
post.description: Re-call after sign-in, Hub switch and on any lv_forbidden/lv_not_member to detect revoked access. Capabilities are advisory. Creates the caller's account on first use (never merged by email). roles and capabilities are empty until the roles migration lands.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Request a data export or account deletion.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Public Hub card by slug, including the caller's viewer status. Private details are never returned.
post.description: A released or unknown slug returns lv_not_found with no information about a previous owner. member_count is null unless the Hub is public or the caller is an accepted member. The existence of a private Hub is visible by slug (decision D-09).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Join, or apply to join, a Hub according to its membership mode.
post.description: Repeating the call returns the existing status. Invite-only Hubs admit only accounts that already have an invitation; A supplied invite_code is refused with lv_policy_undecided and details.reason = invite_code_unsupported, even for an invited account (P-05); account-bound invitations are accepted by calling without a code. Suspended and removed accounts get lv_forbidden.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Accept or reject a pending application.
post.description: Only a pending application can be decided (otherwise lv_conflict). Reject deletes the application so the person may re-apply (provisional). Until the roles migration lands only the Owner holds this capability.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Leave a Hub. The Owner cannot leave without transferring ownership.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Remove a member. The Owner cannot be removed.
post.description: A removed member cannot rejoin (provisional).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Suspend a member (excluded from counts and gates until restored).
post.description: Idempotent for an already suspended member; only an accepted member can be suspended. A suspended member cannot leave or rejoin.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Accepted member count (pending, invited, suspended and guests are excluded).
post.description: A private Hub answers lv_not_found to anyone who is not an accepted member, so its size is not disclosed.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Members with status and roles for people management.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Change Hub name, visibility and membership mode.
post.description: Omitted fields are unchanged; at least one must be given. name is the Hub's v2 display name (1-80 characters, no control characters): it does not edit the legacy organization name, which keeps serving the legacy app. The slug never changes here (D-09). Every real change is audited (before and after). Setting no real MJCC values is deliberate: the Hub's name, visibility and join mode are founder decisions (P-04, P-39).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Delete a Hub. Owner only; never grantable to a role.
post.description: Retention and recovery rules are undecided; the function must not delete data until they are set.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Self-service Hub creation for an APPROVED beta applicant. One transaction creates the Hub (own slug and name), the Owner's accepted membership, the Owner designation and the beta grant, and consumes the approval; all or nothing.
post.description: Fails closed with lv_policy_undecided (details.missing) until beta.terms (the grant length and which plan limits full access means) and slug.reserved are decided. The 50-owner cap is confirmed and counted under a lock. No Owner is ever assigned by a developer: the caller becomes Owner by creating the Hub.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: The grantable capability catalog (three categories) and the Owner-only operations.
post.description: Proposed vocabulary (27 capabilities in three categories; D-02). Owner-only operations (hub.delete, hub.transfer_ownership) are listed in owner_only and can never be granted to a role.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Custom roles of a Hub with slot usage. The protected Owner does not consume a slot.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Create a custom role. Slot limits are enforced under a Hub-level lock.
post.description: Capabilities must be held by the caller (no escalation: lv_forbidden, details.reason = cannot_grant_unheld_capability, details.missing) and must exist in the catalog (hub.* and unknown ids are lv_invalid_input). Starter allows 3 custom roles and Team 6 (Owner excluded), taken from entitlement grants: no active grant is lv_entitlement_missing; a plan whose allowance is undecided is lv_policy_undecided; a full Hub is lv_quota_exceeded with details {limit, used}. Today only synthetic grants exist; no real grant has been issued (P-12).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Rename a role, change its icon or replace its capabilities.
post.description: Omitted or null name/icon/capabilities are left unchanged; icon "" clears the icon. The caller must hold every capability the role already carries (details.reason = role_exceeds_your_authority) and every capability they add (P-07).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Delete a role and its assignments.
post.description: Frees the slot and removes every assignment. The caller must hold every capability the role carries (P-07).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Assign a role to an accepted member. The grantor must hold every capability the role carries.
post.description: Roles belong to one Hub; assigning across Hubs is impossible (a person who is not an accepted member of the role's Hub is lv_not_member). Not assignable to the Owner. Assignments disappear when the member stops being accepted (P-10).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Remove a role from a member.
post.description: lv_not_found when the person does not hold the role. The caller must hold every capability the role carries (P-07).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Enable or disable one capability on a role.
post.description: Enabling needs the caller to hold the capability; editing needs authority over the whole role (P-07). Owner-only ids are lv_invalid_input.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Enable or disable every delegable capability in one category on a role. Never affects Owner-only operations.
post.description: Enabling a category requires the caller to hold every capability in it (no partial grant, P-08); disabling removes all of them.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Owner offers ownership to an accepted member; the offer expires.
post.description: Owner only; no capability or role grants this. Fails closed with lv_policy_undecided until the reauthentication and offer-expiry policy are set (P-11). When the access token lacks a sufficiently fresh authentication the answer is lv_forbidden with details.reason = reauthentication_required: send the person through sign-in again, then retry with the new token. One open offer per Hub (lv_conflict); an expired open offer is expired on the spot. Recipient must be an accepted member (lv_not_member).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Recipient accepts; ownership swaps atomically (never zero or two Owners).
post.description: Only the addressed recipient, with fresh authentication (details.reason = reauthentication_required). One transaction under the Hub lock: stale (Owner changed), expired, cancelled and superseded offers are lv_lifecycle_invalid with details.status; replay by the recipient returns the same result. The previous Owner becomes an ordinary accepted member with no roles; the new Owner's role assignments are dissolved. There is always exactly one Owner.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Owner cancels an open offer.
post.description: The Owner withdraws or the recipient declines. Only a pending offer can be cancelled.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Effective plan, active grants and limit usage for a Hub. A null limit means the policy is undecided, never unlimited. A Hub with no active grant has plan_code null and no grants.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Additional-survey participation gate: numerator, denominator, scope and next action.
post.description: Integer comparisons: Starter strictly more than 50% (2R > M), Team at least 20% (5R >= M), R = distinct eligible accepted members who took part (guests and repeat responses cannot add), M = eligible accepted members. Fails closed with lv_policy_undecided and details.missing when any of these is undecided: gate.measurement (window), gate.eligible_population, gate.applies_to, quota.consuming_states, gate.rule_for_plan (the plan has no decided rule) or gate.bootstrap (only when M = 0) (P-15, P-16). met is true with a "no requirement" next_action when the gate does not apply to the next survey. policy_version is "provisional-" plus a hash of the policy values.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Founder-issued manual entitlement grant (audited). Service role only; no payment involved.
post.description: Grant terms (free, discounted, time-limited) are D-07. This operation records them; it does not choose them.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Create a draft Campaign. Only survey mode is available in M1; other modes return lv_policy_undecided.
post.description: survey is the only available mode (others return lv_policy_undecided, details.decision = D-08); guest_access link returns lv_policy_undecided (D-03). Drafts need no entitlement; the join code (6 characters) is generated now. anonymous is stored but its analytics are policy-pending (D-10).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Campaigns of a Hub, optionally by state.
post.description: Visible to anyone holding community.campaign.draft, .activate or .close. A Campaign past its closing time is listed as expired even before the expiry job persists it. Archived legacy sessions appear here as closed Campaigns with legacy_historical = true and legacy_session_id set; filter or label them in the UI (they are history, not Winter Survey work).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: One Campaign with its share data (join code).
post.description: Visible to anyone holding community.campaign.draft, .activate or .close.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Edit a draft: title, anonymity flag and question set. Active Campaigns are immutable; publish creates a revision.
post.description: Draft only (lv_lifecycle_invalid, details.reason = not_a_draft). Passing questions replaces the whole set and increments the revision; omitted fields are unchanged. required defaults to false; scale defaults to 1..5.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: The published question set for a Campaign the caller may answer, or the draft set for an editor.
post.description: Editors (community.campaign.draft) see any state. Other accepted members see the questions only while the Campaign is active (otherwise lv_lifecycle_invalid). Guests and non-members are not served yet.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Set the opening and closing times (America/New_York is a display concern; values are timestamps with offset).
post.description: Draft or scheduled only. Times are timestamps with offset; nothing here defines the Winter Survey time or timezone (D-12). Scheduling reserves nothing: entitlement, quota, gate and lifecycle are checked again when the Campaign opens (P-19). The person who scheduled it must still hold community.campaign.activate at that moment.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Atomic activation: capability, entitlement, caps, gate and schedule checked under a Hub lock; activation persisted once.
post.description: One atomic path under a Hub-level lock for manual activation, reopening a closed Campaign and scheduled activation: permission, lifecycle, entitlement, quota, gate, in that order. A retry with the same idempotency_key (same actor) returns the first result with replay=true and never restarts a clock; another actor with that key gets lv_conflict; a NEW key on an already active Campaign is lv_lifecycle_invalid (reason already_active). Failures carry details: quota {limit_name, limit, used}; gate {numerator, denominator, plan}; policy {reason, missing}; lifecycle {reason, state}. Responses are never touched by closing, expiry or reopening. An archived record of a legacy session (legacy_historical) is never activatable: lv_lifecycle_invalid with details.reason = legacy_historical (P-42).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Server-derived answer to "can this Campaign be activated now, and if not why": every blocker in priority order plus the quota and gate state to display.
post.description: Read-only and computed by the same function that enforces activation, so it cannot disagree with lv_campaign_activate. The UI displays it; it is never the enforcement authority (activation re-checks everything).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Close an active Campaign. Responses are preserved.
post.description: Active to closed; closing a closed or expired Campaign returns it unchanged; a draft or scheduled one is lv_lifecycle_invalid. Participation records are untouched.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Create a revocable guest share for one Campaign.
post.description: Guest proof, lifespan and abuse limits are D-03. Returns lv_policy_undecided until decided.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Resolve a join code to a Campaign and say whether the caller may participate.
post.description: Codes are case-insensitive. Drafts and scheduled Campaigns never resolve. A private Hub's Campaign resolves only for its accepted members; anyone else, including anon, gets lv_not_found (same as a wrong code). A public Hub's active, closed or expired Campaign resolves for anyone. requires_account is always true until guest proof is decided (P-22). There is no rate limiting yet (abuse limits undecided, P-27).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Submit answers once per participant. Anonymous Campaigns store answers apart from the participation receipt.
post.description: Members only: a non-member, a suspended/removed/pending member, a member of another Hub and an unknown Campaign all get the same lv_not_found. Bound to the Campaign's immutable published question revision; answers are validated server-side (unknown or duplicate question, missing required, number range, option membership, boolean, ranking, text length: lv_invalid_input with details.reason and question_id). Duplicates are decided by person, not by key: any second submission by the same person to the same Campaign, with any idempotency_key and any answers, returns the ORIGINAL receipt with duplicate=true and stores nothing; this also holds after close and after reopening (P-20, P-21). Not open: lv_lifecycle_invalid with details.reason not_active (state) or closed_by_time. Close and submit are serialized on the Campaign row; a submission is wholly accepted or wholly refused, and the closing time is re-read after any lock wait. Non-survey modes: lv_policy_undecided (D-08). Receipt.reward_state is unset unless a reward policy exists, and a recorded reward does not change any balance (P-24). Anonymous Campaigns store answers with no account and no link to the receipt (P-23).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: The caller's own participation receipts. Receipts never reveal answers.
post.description: Only the caller's own receipts (member participation), newest first. No role, including the Owner, can list anyone else's. Guest receipts are not listed.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Privacy-safe aggregates for one Campaign: participation, per-question completion, or one question's answer distribution. Member and guest populations are separate; suppressed values are null, never 0.
post.description: Anonymous Campaigns (and any Campaign with guest responses) return lv_policy_undecided with details.missing until THREE policy values are set: analytics.min_cohort, analytics.min_participants and analytics.disclosure_controls; a threshold alone does not settle D-10. Even then they are served only after the Campaign has finished (reason live_anonymous_results_restricted) and only for one population size: the first release freezes the participant counts and later changes make the results unavailable (reason population_changed_after_release), which blocks differencing between releases (P-28 to P-30). Query shapes are deliberately restricted: no filters, cross-tabulations, time slices or free text; text and ranking questions return lv_policy_undecided. Draft and scheduled Campaigns are lv_lifecycle_invalid. Identified (non-anonymous) Campaigns without guests need no privacy policy and may be read live (policy.status not_required). A cell with 0 < n < min_cohort is suppressed; suppressed or withheld values are null with suppressed = true and a reason, never 0; a real zero is 0. Every call is logged. There is no export or embed path. Archived legacy sessions (legacy_historical) return lv_policy_undecided with details.reason = legacy_record_policy_pending whatever the analytics policy says (P-44).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Create an aggregate export. Raw anonymous rows are never exportable.
post.description: Blocked: retention, export format and small-group rules (D-10) are undecided. No export path exists, and none will be added before they are decided.

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Join the public beta waitlist.
post.description: Closed until the founder decides FOUR things: waitlist.open, waitlist.consent_version (the approved wording), waitlist.retention and waitlist.removal. While anything is missing the answer is lv_policy_undecided with details.missing; a deliberately closed list answers status closed. WHAT IS STORED: the private waitlist table keeps the normalized email address, the optional intended Hub name, the consent version shown and a deletion date (personal data; no API access, no read-back operation, no link to any account or Hub). The throttle ledger keeps only SALTED HASHES of the address and of the caller origin, never raw addresses or IPs, and is cleared after 7 days. NO ENUMERATION: a new and a repeat sign-up (any case or spacing) answer identically (queued), the status duplicate is never returned, and the throttle counts only the caller's own attempts from the caller's own origin, so what a caller sees never depends on what anyone else submitted (tested against a different origin). ORIGIN: the network address is used only if waitlist.trusted_ip names a header and a proxy-hop count counted from the RIGHT, i.e. the entry appended by your own proxies; a value supplied by the browser is never trusted by itself, and with no trusted source configured every caller shares one bucket. It must be verified against the real edge before the list opens. Provisional, unapproved limits: 5 attempts per address per origin per day and 30 per origin per hour (lv_rate_limited with details.retry_after_seconds). Operator functions purge expired rows and perform removal requests. Consent copy, retention length and the removal channel are founder decisions (P-37, P-38).

200.description: Envelope: success, or a failure with a stable error code.

post.summary: Apply to run a beta Hub. Needs a signed-in person with a verified email; one open application per person; repeating returns the open one.
post.description: Distinct from the public waitlist: nothing here reads or writes it. The contact email is taken from the verified token and is shown only to platform reviewers.

serviceRole.description: Server-side only. Never ship to a browser.

RequestId.description: Server-generated id echoed in every v2 response; quote it in support requests.

Slug.description: Hub address segment (lunchvoice.com/{slug}). Matching is case-insensitive. Full naming and reserved-word rules are decision D-09 and are not defined here.

details.description: Machine-readable context, for example limit/used for lv_quota_exceeded or numerator/denominator for lv_gate_unmet.

limit.description: null means the limit is undecided (never treat as unlimited).

capabilities.description: Advisory list for UI hints. The server re-checks every action.

member_count.description: Accepted members only; pending, invited, suspended and guests never count. null when the Hub is private and the caller is not an accepted member.

owner_only.description: Operations that no role can grant (delete Hub, transfer ownership).

undecided.description: Limit names whose policy is still undecided (for example Team totals). Their limit is null.

CampaignMode.description: Only survey is in scope for M1. Other modes are M2 and their contracts are decision D-08.

GuestAccess.description: link requires decision D-03 (guest proof). Until decided the server rejects it with lv_policy_undecided.

details.description: Same shape as Error.details for that code, for example {limit_name, limit, used} for lv_quota_exceeded or {missing: [...]} for lv_policy_undecided.

missing.description: Policy keys that are undecided; when non-empty the other fields are null (fail closed).

blockers.description: Every reason activation would fail now, in the order the server checks them. Empty when can_activate is true.

QuestionType.description: rating, text, single_choice, multi_choice, yes_no, flame and slider exist in production today (survey_questions_type_check). nps and ranking are v2 additions (M2 unless the Winter Survey questionnaire needs them; D-12).

value.description: Any JSON value valid for the question type.

points.description: null unless a reward policy exists. A recorded reward does not change any balance.

reward_state.description: unset: no reward policy has been decided (never 0). recorded: points recorded on the receipt by a decided policy. not_applicable: guests.

reason.description: Why n is null: below_min_participants. Null when shown.

key.description: Question id (completion), option label or rating value (answer_distribution).

n.description: null when suppressed. A shown 0 is a real zero.

reason.description: below_min_cohort, complementary or below_min_participants when suppressed.

value.description: Share of that audience's participants, 4 decimals; null when suppressed.

population.description: Plain-language definition of who is counted. Display it next to the numbers.

min_cohort.description: The cell threshold in force when status is applied; null when not_required.

content.description: Sanitised block content; format is decision D-11.

status.description: queued for a new or repeat sign-up (indistinguishable by design); closed when the waitlist is deliberately closed. duplicate is reserved and never returned, so the response cannot be used to find out who is on the list.

note.description: Optional free text about the Hub they plan to run.

MenuSyncResult.description: sync-menu returns { cycle_id, days_synced, source_anchor_date, synced_at }; sync-feedback returns { rows_pushed }.

LegacyString.description: Session id, or a human-readable message such as "Session not found or closed." / "ok".

x-provisional-register.summary: Rejecting a pending application deletes it (the audit trail keeps the event), so the person may apply again immediately. No cool-down, reason or block list.
A removed member cannot rejoin by themselves (lv_forbidden). Whether removal is permanent, time-limited or reversible by an admin is undecided; there is no reinstate operation.
The existence, name and join mode of a private Hub are visible to anyone who knows its slug (needed for the private-Hub gate). Its member count is hidden from non-members.
Membership defaults: a Hub created by the backfill is private and invite-only. These are database column defaults, not MJCC's settings, and must be set explicitly for every real Hub before launch.

Invite codes are unsupported: a supplied code is refused with lv_policy_undecided (details.reason = invite_code_unsupported), even for an account that holds an account-bound invitation. Account-bound invitations (status invited) are accepted by calling lv_join_hub without a code. Code generation, redemption, expiry and revocation are undecided.

Every legacy member of an organization becomes an accepted member of its Hub (backfill, signup mirror, repair), including students who have never used v2. Whether legacy accounts count as valid members for gates and discovery is undecided.

Delegation: nobody can grant a capability they do not hold, and a non-Owner can edit, assign, unassign or delete a role only if they hold every capability that role carries. The founder has not decided how far role managers may reach (for example whether they may manage peers or lesser roles they only partly cover).
Enabling a whole capability category on a role requires holding every capability in it; there is no partial group grant. Disabling a category needs only authority over the role.
A non-Owner can remove or suspend only a member whose capabilities are within their own. Whether peers or lesser roles may act on each other is undecided.

A member may hold several roles. Role assignments are dropped automatically when a membership stops being accepted (suspended, removed, left) and do not return on reinstatement. The Owner holds no roles (authority is direct); becoming Owner dissolves existing assignments.

Owner transfer reauthentication (required method and maximum age) and offer lifetime are UNDECIDED and unset in the database, so lv_owner_transfer_start/accept fail closed with lv_policy_undecided. When set, the database checks the amr claim of the access token; that does not prove the Google or central-identity reauthentication flow, which is a separate integration (D-01) with its own verification.

Custom role slots (Starter 3, Team 6, Owner excluded) are confirmed numbers, but they are read from entitlement grants and no real grant exists: a Hub without an active grant cannot create roles, a plan whose allowance is undecided (campaign plans, manual) answers lv_policy_undecided, and what happens when a downgrade leaves more roles than slots is undefined.

The capability vocabulary (27 ids in Administration, Hub Appearance & Structure, Community & Campaigns) is a proposal. `community.moderate` was renamed `community.comments.moderate`. Ids may change before launch; the roles migration seeds them from a table, not code.

Which Campaign states consume an active-Campaign slot is UNDECIDED (only active? also scheduled?). Activation fails closed (lv_policy_undecided, missing quota.consuming_states) until set. The `used` numbers shown in lv_entitlements and lv_campaign_activation_status count Campaigns that are currently active only.

The participation gate's measurement window, eligible population, and which survey it first applies to (for example the second active survey) are UNDECIDED and unset. Only the comparisons are confirmed (Starter strictly above 50%, Team at least 20%, unique eligible accepted members, exact integers). Test values are illustrative and not policy.
Gate result when the eligible population is empty (bootstrap) is UNDECIDED; it fails closed with missing gate.bootstrap rather than defaulting to met or unmet.
Team page and active-Campaign totals are UNDECIDED and stay null (never unlimited). Because activation needs a decided total, a Team-only Hub cannot activate any Campaign until D-06 sets it.
Beta, manual and Campaign-plan grants carry no decided limits, so they activate nothing: beta access is not assumed to be a free paid tier. A Hub with no active grant gets lv_entitlement_missing.

Lifecycle rules chosen for testability: only drafts are editable; a Campaign expires when its closing time passes and cannot be reopened; a closed one can reopen until then; scheduling reserves nothing and every check is repeated when it opens; the scheduler must still hold the capability. Only survey mode exists. Nothing defines the Winter Survey opening time, timezone, closing, operator, questionnaire, audience or anonymity (D-12). The job that runs scheduled activations and expiry is an operator function with no scheduler configured.

Duplicate rule: one response per person per Campaign, decided by person and independent of the idempotency key. A second attempt (same key, new key, different answers) returns the ORIGINAL receipt with duplicate = true and stores nothing; the first answers win. Whether a person may ever resubmit or amend is undecided.

Reopening a closed Campaign does NOT let a person who already responded respond again; people who had not responded may. Whether reopening should allow a new response is undecided and there is deliberately no code path for it.

Guests: no public entry point exists. The storage and a scoped, revocable grant exist and are tested internally, but guest proof, how grants are issued, their lifespan and abuse limits are undecided, and guest_access = link cannot be set. Guests never become members, never get a reward and never see Hub data.

Anonymous Campaign storage: answers carry no account and no reference to the receipt, only a calendar date; database guards refuse to write either link. Residual risk: someone with direct database access (not the API roles) can still correlate rows through transaction metadata. Retention, who may have such access, and whether this meets the Winter Survey's anonymity promise are undecided.

Rewards: no points are invented. Receipts say reward_state unset (points null) until a reward policy is decided; a recorded reward is only a number on the receipt and changes no legacy or v2 balance. Applying rewards to the points ledger is undecided.
Audience: any accepted member of the Campaign's Hub may respond. Narrower audiences (roles, groups, invitations) are undecided and not implemented.

Answer limits chosen for safety: at most 100 answers, text up to 2000 characters, optional questions may be left out, a required question needs a non-empty answer. The real questionnaire is undecided.
Join-code resolution has no rate limiting or lockout, and private-Hub codes resolve only for accepted members. Abuse limits for public codes are undecided.

Anonymous (and guest-bearing) analytics need THREE undecided policy values before anything is shown: a cell threshold (analytics.min_cohort), a minimum participant total (analytics.min_participants) and the disclosure controls (analytics.disclosure_controls). Approving a number alone does not settle D-10; the other controls, retention and export rules remain open.

Anonymous results are served only after the Campaign has finished, never live, to stop a trickle of new responses revealing individual answers. Whether live anonymous results should ever be shown is undecided.

Single release: the first release of sensitive results freezes the participant counts; if responses change afterwards (for example after a reopening) the results become unavailable rather than risk differencing between two releases. How repeat releases, corrections and late responses should work is undecided.

Restricted query shapes: one Campaign, one metric, optionally one question. No filters, no cross-tabulation, no time slicing, no per-response timestamps, no free-text or ranking results. These stay closed until small-group disclosure rules for each shape are approved.

Complementary suppression is a configurable control, not a decided rule: when set, a single suppressed cell in a partitioning distribution also withholds the smallest remaining cell. Whether to also round, bucket or hide totals is undecided.
Members and guests are separate populations with separate thresholds and are never combined into one number. Whether guest results may be shown to the Hub at all is undecided.

Identified (non-anonymous) Campaigns without guests are shown with exact counts and no privacy policy, because the Hub already holds who answered. Whether identified aggregates need any minimum is undecided.
Export and embed are blocked: no operation exports or embeds results, raw or aggregate, until retention, format and small-group rules are decided and an entitlement is defined.

The public waitlist is closed until the founder decides four things: waitlist.open, the consent wording (waitlist.consent_version), the retention period (waitlist.retention) and the removal channel (waitlist.removal). Opening alone is not enough. Who is admitted and the confirmed 50-beta-owner cap are separate, unimplemented decisions; joining the waitlist promises nothing.

Waitlist consent and legal wording are undecided. Each sign-up stores the version of the approved wording that was shown, but engineering has not written or approved any wording; see contract/WAITLIST_PROPOSAL.md for a proposal that needs founder and legal review.

Waitlist retention and removal are undecided. The table holds the email address (personal data) with a deletion date from the retention policy, no API access and no read-back operation; an operator purge and an operator removal function exist and are tested. The throttle ledger holds salted hashes only and is cleared after 7 days. How long to keep addresses, who may export them and how people request removal are founder decisions.

The waitlist throttle values (5 attempts per address per origin per day, 30 per origin per hour) are PROVISIONAL TEST VALUES, not approved. They count only the caller's own attempts, so they cannot reveal prior submissions by others.

A Hub's v2 display name is stored separately from the legacy organization name and never overwrites it. Who may rename, and the naming and reserved-word rules, are undecided (D-09); only length and control characters are checked.

Trusted network identity for the waitlist is NOT configured (waitlist.trusted_ip unset), so every caller shares one throttle bucket. When set it uses the entry N places from the right of a named proxy header, which only holds if the production edge (Render/Supabase/Cloudflare) is verified to append the real client address there; a browser-supplied value is never trusted. The header name and hop count must be confirmed against the live edge before the list opens.

Legacy bridge scope: only HISTORICAL legacy survey sessions (not live, not menu-rating, no ambiguity) become archived, closed Campaigns marked legacy_historical. They never consume a quota slot, never count toward the participation gate, cannot be activated, reopened, edited or answered. Live sessions stay in the legacy app until a separately authorized cutover; menu-rating sessions stay legacy-only.

Nothing is invented for archived records: they are identified (legacy responses kept the respondent id), guest access is off, opening and closing times are copied exactly as stored (a session with a backwards window is held as ambiguous, not repaired), the question set is revision 1 exactly as the legacy template stands today (the legacy app lets templates be edited, so the set may differ from what respondents saw), and points are recorded as awarded, not re-applied.

Results for archived legacy sessions are unavailable (policy-pending) regardless of any analytics policy: there is no evidence of what respondents were told about anonymity or publication, so none is assumed.

Ambiguous legacy records (no template, missing template, no questions, impossible scale or prompt length, title length, backwards time window, empty or colliding join code) are never mapped, repaired or discarded: they are listed with a reason for a human decision. Responses by students without an account or from another organization are held back and listed, not dropped.

Legacy transition: legacy RPCs, login and surveys keep running untouched. The bridge is repeatable and per-session atomic; responses and answers that arrive later are picked up by the next sync; reconciliation reports drift (for example a mapped session live again). Rolling the bridge back deletes only the derived archive; every legacy row and every native v2 Campaign is unaffected. Nothing schedules the sync.

Hub creation (lv_hub_create) fails closed with lv_policy_undecided until two founder decisions exist: beta.terms (the grant length in months, which is confirmed as three, and which plan's limits 'full access' means) and slug.reserved (the reserved-address list). The 50-owner cap is confirmed and enforced under a lock. The beta grant starts at Hub creation, which is the recommended default and is NOT founder-approved.

Platform reviewers (who may decide beta applications) are rows in this database's platform_admins table, granted only by audited operator functions. Whether that authority should instead come from a claim issued by the central KpnIdentity platform is undecided; until then there must be exactly one source, and this table is it. Nobody can decide their own application.

A person is the pair (issuer, subject) from a verified token. The issuer allow-list (identity.trusted_issuers) ships unset, the subject must be a UUID, and email/name claims are display and verification inputs only. The real KpnIdentity issuer, subject format and claim names are unverified assumptions; an email must be marked verified by the token before a beta application is accepted.
